summary: Adds a shared repository-lifecycle guard for retired EE and prevents workflow-plugin tests from selecting unrelated heavyweight CI lanes.
userImpact: EnterpriseGlue status, CI, dependency, release, deployment, and implementation workflows no longer include standalone EE unless a read-only historical audit is explicitly requested.
Workflow-plugin-only changes use contract and policy validation without selecting host release readiness or unrelated application, database, browser, and image matrices.

instructions: Reinstall the EnterpriseGlue development-workflows plugin and remove legacy personal EnterpriseGlue skill copies that shadow it.

security: The lifecycle guard blocks accidental write, release, synchronization, and deployment actions against the archived EE repository.
documentation: Updates the versioned Codex workflow plugin guide with lifecycle-registry and personal-skill precedence guidance.
knownLimitations: Repositories not listed in the core lifecycle registry continue to be routed by their owning workflow and repository instructions.
rollback: Revert the workflow-plugin change; reactivating the EE repository remains a separate explicitly authorized governance decision.
validation: Codex plugin tests assert that retired EE is blocked for status, CI, dependencies, release, deployment, and writes, while explicit historical reads remain available.

CI classifier fixtures assert that workflow-plugin tests use the developer-workflow fast path and do not fan out to host release readiness, PostgreSQL, Oracle, application-image, plugin-image, tenancy, backstop, identity, or deployment lanes.
